slots.label: Heading 1
slots.default: The test is the restore, not the backup

slots.label: Paragraph 1
slots.default: Backups fail quietly. They run, they report success, and the problem only shows up on the day someone needs a file back. That is why the measure worth caring about is whether a restore has actually been performed recently, not whether the job is green.

slots.label: Paragraph 2
slots.default: What we look for is granular recovery, so a single message or one folder can come back without restoring an entire account; coverage across Gmail, Drive, Shared Drives, Contacts and Calendar rather than mail alone; a retention period long enough that a deletion noticed months later is still recoverable; and a copy held independently of the Workspace tenant, so a compromise of the tenant cannot reach it.

slots.label: Paragraph 3
slots.default: Two practical questions are worth asking of any arrangement, including ours: how far back can you go, and how long would a realistic recovery take. If nobody can answer both, the position is not yet a backup. If you also run Microsoft, the same reasoning applies there and is covered by
